name: Meta Platforms, Inc.
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Meta is running the steepest AI-infrastructure escalation of any hyperscaler — capex guidance of $130–145B for 2026 (vs $39B actual in 2024), multi-gigawatt named campuses (Hyperion at 5 GW/$50B+, Prometheus ~1 GW, El Paso ~1 GW), and up to 6.6 GW of contracted nuclear — funded off-balance-sheet through JVs with Blue Owl and BlackRock while free cash flow collapsed to under $1B a quarter; it is the only member of the big four with no external cloud/AI revenue line to absorb the spend. BACKGROUND: Founded 2004; Family of Apps (3.60B daily users; ~98% of revenue is advertising), Reality Labs (Quest/Ray-Ban glasses, ~$4.6B quarterly losses), Meta Superintelligence Labs (Alexandr Wang, formed 2025), Llama models, and MTIA custom inference silicon. FY2025 revenue $200.97B (+22%), net income $60.46B.
ecosystemRole: We assess Meta as the ecosystem's most aggressive single energy buyer relative to its size: >30 GW of clean energy contracted, ~7.7 GW of nuclear (Constellation Clinton 1.1 GW + the January 2026 TerraPower/Oklo/Vistra package of up to 6.6 GW), seven new gas plants plus three grid-scale batteries in the Entergy Louisiana package, and frontier bets (1 GW/100 GWh Noon Energy long-duration storage reservation; 1 GW space solar). Its BESS exposure runs through utility-side tolled storage (Enbridge Cowboy: 200 MW/1,600 MWh Tesla batteries) rather than on-campus deployment — no evidence of behind-the-meter BESS at Hyperion or Prometheus.

productsAndServices.name: AI Infrastructure & Superclusters
productsAndServices.description: Named multi-GW campuses: Hyperion (Richland Parish, LA — 5 GW design, $50B+, ~2,250 acres, first multi-gigawatt AI training cluster; ~2 GW by 2030), Prometheus (New Albany, OH — ~1 GW supercluster, online 2026), El Paso TX (~1 GW by 2028), Lebanon IN (1 GW, $10B+), Kansas City (operational). Financing model: SPV/JV structures — Blue Owl (Hyperion: ~$27B, 80/20, $26B PIMCO debt) and BlackRock (El Paso: ~$14B, 80/20) — moving the build off Meta's balance sheet.
highlights: Capex trajectory: $39.2B (2024) → $72.2B (2025) → $130–145B guided (2026), raised twice during 2026
Q2 2026 capex $31.1B consumed ~98% of operating cash flow; FCF fell to $784M (−91% YoY)
MTIA custom inference silicon deployed across 16 regions for ranking/ads; a reported multi-year Google TPU lease (confirmed at ~$10B Google Cloud agreement level) diversifies compute
Llama 4 line (Scout/Maverick/Behemoth ~2T params) plus the first Meta Superintelligence Labs model (Q1 2026)
productsAndServices.positioning: Steepest YoY capex increase among the big four and the only one with no external AI/cloud revenue — Meta's return path is ads improvement and future superintelligence products, which is why its prints draw the most ROI skepticism (stock fell on both 2026 guidance raises)
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Internal capacity (no cloud resale); financed via JV lease structures
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Own AI training/inference for ads, apps, and superintelligence research
productsAndServices.roadmap: Hyperion full build ~2032; El Paso online 2028; first AI-optimized DC online 2026

productsAndServices.name: Energy Procurement Portfolio
productsAndServices.category: Power · what this app's readers sell into
productsAndServices.description: Over 30 GW of clean energy contracted; 100% renewable-matched since 2020. Nuclear: Constellation Clinton (1,121 MW, 20-yr, from 2027) plus the January 2026 package — TerraPower (2 Natrium units of 690 MW each + rights to six more, with 1.2 GW of molten-salt thermal storage capability), Oklo (up to 1.2 GW Aurora campus, ~2030), Vistra (2.1 GW existing-plant PPAs + 433 MW uprates, the largest corporate-backed uprates). Gas: seven new plants (~5.2 GW Phase 2 proposal + ~2.3 GW Phase 1) with Entergy Louisiana for Hyperion. Storage: three grid-scale batteries in the Entergy package; 50 MW/4-hr BESS paired with 190 MW NM solar; Enbridge Cowboy (365 MW solar + 200 MW/1,600 MWh Tesla BESS, tolled via the Wyoming utility); Noon Energy LDES reservation up to 1 GW/100 GWh (>100-hr, pilot 2028). PPAs: Invenergy (1,800 MW cumulative), AES (650 MW), Sage/XGS geothermal (300 MW combined), Overview space solar (up to 1 GW, ~2030).
highlights: ~7.7 GW total contracted nuclear — the largest corporate nuclear commitment

The Louisiana gas build-out is the ecosystem's highest-profile ratepayer controversy: LPSC challenges, a judge ordering Meta to reveal withheld demand evidence, and 15-yr Meta contracts vs 30-yr plant lives flagged by a dissenting commissioner
Storage posture: utility-side tolling and portfolio PPAs, not on-campus BESS — a gap suppliers pitch against
productsAndServices.positioning: Second-largest corporate clean-energy buyer cohort with Amazon (combined 20.4 GW contracted in 2025 per BNEF); distinctive for frontier-technology reservations (LDES, space solar, Natrium storage)
productsAndServices.soldThrough: PPAs, utility tariffs (Entergy/ratepayer-protection pledge), tolling agreements, JV development
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Counterparties: utilities, IPPs, nuclear developers, storage developers
productsAndServices.roadmap: TerraPower units ~2032; Oklo ~2030; Noon pilot 2028; Entergy Phase 2 under LPSC review

productsAndServices.name: Family of Apps & Reality Labs

Reality Labs: Quest headsets and Ray-Ban Meta glasses with persistent ~$4.6B quarterly operating losses; ~8,000-role reduction in May 2026 partly aimed at Reality Labs and framed as funding the AI pivot.

recentDevelopments.headline: Q2 2026: revenue $60.8B (+28%) beat; EPS $6.18 missed ~$7.22 consensus on a 55% cost jump ($2.4B legal, $1.18B severance); capex floor raised to $130B; FCF $784M
recentDevelopments.read: The quarter that crystallized the bear case: ads can fund the buildout, but free cash flow is gone and the market repriced accordingly (−8–10% after hours).

recentDevelopments.headline: BlackRock JV for the ~1 GW El Paso campus (~$14B, 80/20, $12.5B debt; Meta receives ~$1B distribution)
recentDevelopments.read: The Blue Owl playbook repeated — Meta is industrializing off-balance-sheet AI-campus finance, keeping guidance-capex lower than economic capex.

recentDevelopments.headline: Richland Parish (Hyperion) expanded to 5 GW / $50B+; Entergy package confirmed: seven new gas plants + three grid-scale batteries + nuclear uprates
recentDevelopments.read: The single largest AI-campus commitment in the covered set — and the one carrying the most regulatory and ratepayer friction.

recentDevelopments.headline: Enbridge Cowboy Phase 1 (Wyoming): 365 MW solar + 200 MW/1,600 MWh Tesla-battery BESS serving Meta data centers via utility tolling (~$1.2B Enbridge investment)
recentDevelopments.read: Meta's clearest BESS-linked deal — structured so the utility tolls the battery; Meta partnership with Enbridge now totals 1.6 GW.

recentDevelopments.headline: Frontier energy reservations: Noon Energy LDES up to 1 GW/100 GWh (>100-hr; 25 MW pilot 2028) and Overview space solar up to 1 GW (~2030)
recentDevelopments.read: Meta is buying options on post-lithium duration classes — a signal to LDES developers that hyperscaler demand extends beyond 4-hour BESS.

recentDevelopments.headline: CoreWeave agreement expanded to ~$21B through December 2032 — dedicated multi-site capacity including early NVIDIA Vera Rubin deployments
recentDevelopments.read: Meta's inference demand is now underwriting the neocloud tier's largest contracts — the ~$19B backlog even collateralizes CoreWeave's SPV debt.

recentDevelopments.headline: Nebius agreement expanded to up to ~$27B over five years — $12B of dedicated Vera Rubin capacity (deliveries from early 2027) plus up to $15B of additional compute
recentDevelopments.read: Second giant neocloud offtake in five months — Meta is dual-sourcing dedicated capacity the way it dual-sources GCs.

recentDevelopments.headline: Up to 6.6 GW of nuclear contracted: TerraPower (Natrium, ~2032), Oklo (~2030), Vistra (2.1 GW + 433 MW uprates)
recentDevelopments.read: The largest corporate nuclear package — Natrium's built-in 1.2 GW thermal-storage capability is the adjacent-storage angle worth tracking.

recentDevelopments.headline: NextEra: ~2.5 GW across 11 PPAs plus two direct energy-storage agreements (168 MW New Mexico, CODs 2026-2028)
recentDevelopments.read: Storage contracted directly with a hyperscaler in ESA format — power procurement moving up the stack alongside the compute deals.

recentDevelopments.headline: Q3 2025: revenue beat but a one-time $15.93B non-cash tax charge and 'notably larger 2026 capex' warning triggered a ~11% selloff
recentDevelopments.read: The first market rebellion against the spending curve — every subsequent print has been judged against capex first, earnings second.

recentDevelopments.headline: Blue Owl JV: ~$27B Hyperion development financing (80/20; $26B PIMCO debt; 4-yr leases + 16-yr residual guarantee)
recentDevelopments.read: The template deal for AI-campus SPV finance — private credit is now load-bearing in hyperscale AI.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess Meta is the highest-beta energy buyer in the covered set: no cloud revenue absorbs the spend, so its $130–145B capex and 6.6 GW nuclear package are bets that superintelligence-era products monetize — the FCF collapse to sub-$1B quarters is the measurable cost of that bet. Basis: filings and guidance evolution.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the SPV/JV financing model (Blue Owl, BlackRock — ~$41B of announced development cost moved off-balance-sheet) is now core strategy: it preserves reported capex optics and credit capacity while transferring residual-value risk to private capital; expect it on every subsequent gigawatt campus.

(Moderate confidence) We assess Meta's storage demand will remain utility-side rather than on-campus near-term: the Entergy batteries, the Enbridge tolling structure, and the absence of behind-the-meter BESS at its flagship campuses point to Meta buying grid firmness as a service — the sales channel for BESS suppliers is Meta's utility counterparties, not Meta directly.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the Louisiana gas controversy is the sector's regulatory bellwether: a judge compelling demand-evidence disclosure and commissioner dissent over stranded-asset risk are the template arguments that will follow every multi-GW campus — outcomes here shape how much firm generation vs storage gets built for AI load.

(Low confidence) The reported Google TPU purchase discussions (beyond the confirmed ~$10B cloud lease) are unconfirmed — if realized from 2027, they would mark the first hyperscaler-to-hyperscaler silicon dependency at scale.

relationships.note: ~$21B expanded AI infrastructure agreement through December 2032.
relationships.context: The initial ~$14.2B agreement (September 2025) was expanded to ~$21B in April 2026 — dedicated capacity across multiple sites for Meta inference workloads, including early NVIDIA Vera Rubin deployments. The ~$19B Meta backlog even serves as collateral support in CoreWeave's March 2026 $8.5B SPV debt facility.

relationships.note: Up to ~$27B over five years — $12B of dedicated Vera Rubin capacity plus a $15B compute option.
relationships.context: The ~$3B November 2025 deal (capped only by Nebius's sold-out capacity) was expanded in March 2026 to up to ~$27B: $12B of dedicated capacity across multiple locations on the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform (deliveries from early 2027) plus commitment to purchase up to $15B of additional compute from upcoming Nebius clusters.

relationships.note: ~2.5 GW across 11 PPAs plus two direct energy-storage agreements (168 MW New Mexico).
relationships.context: December 8, 2025: Meta signed ~2.5 GW with NEER — 11 power purchase agreements plus two energy storage agreements including 168 MW of New Mexico storage (CODs 2026-2028). Storage contracted directly with the hyperscaler in ESA format — power procurement running as deep as the compute contracts.

relationships.note: Co-prime on the ~$50B/5 GW Richland Parish campus and the $10B Lebanon, IN campus.
relationships.context: Turner shares Meta's largest programs: Richland Parish, LA — won at $10B in December 2024 with DPR and Mortenson, expanded to ~$50B / 5 GW / ~10M sq ft by July 2026 (~7,500 peak workers) — plus the $10B, 1 GW Lebanon, Indiana campus and Jeffersonville. Meta standardizes on a repeat builder bench and multi-sources every gigacampus.

relationships.note: Shared-bench prime on Richland Parish and the newest mega-campus wave.
relationships.context: DPR sits on the Turner + DPR + Mortenson team Meta selected for Richland Parish in December 2024 — the shared-bench delivery template now spanning Meta's record Louisiana and Indiana programs.

relationships.note: Three live engagements: Richland Parish power scopes, Lebanon IN co-prime, Beaver Dam WI solo GC.
relationships.context: Mortenson holds the sitework, MV-power, substation, water and fiber scopes on Richland Parish alongside Turner and DPR, a >$10B co-prime at Lebanon, Indiana, and the $1B Beaver Dam, Wisconsin dry-cooled campus as solo GC (completion 2027) — the power-scope specialist on Meta's bench.

relationships.note: Two solar PPAs — Arche (133 MW OH) and Mowata (172 MWdc LA), framed against the Hyperion AI campus.
relationships.context: Meta holds two Lightsource bp offtakes: Arche in Ohio and the $237M Mowata PPA in Acadia Parish, Louisiana (July 2026), which trade press frames against Meta's Hyperion AI campus in Richland Parish — renewable supply siting next to the AI load.

relationships.note: 120 MWac Oregon solar built with Avangrid, PGE and QTS.
relationships.context: December 2024: Avangrid and Portland General Electric collaborated with QTS and Meta on a 120 MWac Oregon solar build — a joint renewable-procurement structure between the hyperscaler and the wholesale landlord.
